happening.text: The party takes the miller's count and runs the first two sluices of the race.
happening.subject: npc/miller

npc/miller.doing: Standing at the tide line watching his wheel run free, counting the sluices aloud out of habit — six and two, three and four — because his hands can no longer do anything else with the number.

happening.text: The party learns the count: three gates, and how long each one gives.
happening.subject: npc/miller

objectives.title: Through the Grate
objectives.hint: North from the tide line, into the sluice house. The iron grate lifts and drops on a count — stand off, watch it once, then walk.

happening.text: The party clears the first sluice and stands inside the sluice house.
happening.subject: anchor/l1a-ward

objectives.title: Down to the Wheel Pit
objectives.hint: Follow the falling water out of the sluice house down to the pit where the wheel is turning. The sluice above it keeps half the count the grate did.

happening.text: The party clears the wheel sluice and drops into the pit, where the undertow takes them under the sea wall.
happening.subject: anchor/l3-landing

obj/hail.text: Somewhere below the yard the wheel is running free — no load, no brake, a hollow knocking that comes faster every turn.

obj/grate.text: You did not guess that gate. You read it. The next one gives you half the window.

obj/wheelpit.text: The pit floor gives way to open water and the undertow takes you, out under the sea wall and down. Nobody swims back up a mill race.

happening.text: The party crosses the tide gate and throws the brake; the wheel is stilled and the mill stands.
happening.subject: anchor/gate

npc/miller.doing: Left far behind and above, still on the tide line with the sea between him and the party, calling the count down a race nobody can hear him from any more.

barks: Six and two. Three and four. Under two — go.
I'd run it myself if these knees were worth their keep.
Grain's in there. Whole village's winter, in there.

objectives.title: The Keeper's Mark
objectives.hint: Wade out of the spill room and stand on the worn flagstone facing the last gate — the mark the keepers stood on to count it.

happening.text: The party reads the keeper's mark and learns what the last gate costs a slow crossing.
happening.subject: anchor/gate

objectives.title: Throw the Brake
objectives.hint: Through the last gate and up into the loft beyond it; the brake lever stands at the head of the room.

happening.text: The party reaches the brake loft past the tide gate and hauls the lever over.
happening.subject: anchor/objective

obj/read.text: The last gate is not the grate. It stands open under two seconds, and it does not shove — it comes down through whatever is standing in it. Count it from here. Do not count it from inside.

happening.text: The brake bites, the wheel stops, and the mill is still standing over the village's grain.
happening.subject: anchor/objective
